title: Minimax Welfare Regret with Dense Surrogates and Rare Target-Reward Audits
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded tier subfield under the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, salvageable=false; analytic interior characterization and substantive application remain open.
gap_reasons: Its “exact minimax value” is delivered computationally through convergent certified programs, not through an analytic value or saddle characterization; the exact large-audit constant, least-favorable support, analytic rule, and arbitrary finite-intensity strictness remain open, so the contribution does not justify a frontier-level or flagship interpretation.

The highly localized binary triangular model and lack of a substantive empirical or design application limit significance at a leading econometrics journal despite the genuine field-level decision-theoretic result.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the two-way original-record transfer, exact four-to-two count pooling, certified finite decision programs, and a matched c⁻¹ audit frontier, with an acknowledged open interior saddle question. The cold D0.5 paper-score gate capped the work at subfield (7.3 versus the field threshold 7.4), so the run stopped before Lean formalization. The local uniform-ledger quantifier and unused bibliography entries were repaired in the versioned source after the terminal review; those cleanup edits were not re-reviewed.
tldr: The audit probability and the surrogate-mismatch probability are both localized at order \(n^{-1/2}\), so audited mismatches remain Poisson rather than vanishing or becoming Gaussian. In a balanced randomized study with a dense binary surrogate and rare target-reward audits, parameter-independent kernels transfer all-procedure root-\(n\) welfare regret to a Gaussian--Poisson limit, and four marks pool exactly to two decision-relevant counts. A fully specified finite primal--dual hierarchy uses \(m^{-1}\)-nets, Gaussian bins of width \(m^{-1}\), the cutoff \(T_m=H+m\), and the count cutoff \(K_m=m+\lceil cU/2\rceil\); explicit interpolation and reconstruction ledgers give certified values and deployable original-record rules. The audit frontier is nonincreasing and continuous, has exact zero- and infinite-audit endpoints, and its excess above the infinite-audit endpoint is exactly of order \(c^{-1}\): a positive-baseline two-point prior gives lower constant \(2Ua_H^2\phi(a_H)\), while the plug-in upper bound supplies an explicit finite constant. Moreover, \(V(c,H,U)>\kappa_H\) for every finite \(c\ge0\), so the infinite-audit endpoint is approached but never attained at finite intensity. The joint signal is strictly better than either single signal both on the finite certified neighborhood around \((1,2,2)\) and throughout an explicit sufficiently-high-audit region. The sharp asymptotic constant, least-favorable support geometry, and strictness between arbitrary finite audit intensities remain open.
gap: Manski and Stoye study minimax-regret treatment choice with incomplete or missing outcome data, and the Gaussian local treatment-choice literature supplies the no-audit benchmark, but these works do not provide the dense-surrogate and rare-audit triangular experiment, its finite Poisson disagreement marks, a compact-uniform two-way full-record experiment comparison with explicit zero-face-valid debits, or the mixed Gaussian--Poisson exact minimax frontier on \(c\in[0,\infty)\). Limited-outcome surrogate work instead studies regular efficiency or gradient variance.
fill: The project defines the Gaussian--Poisson experiment and its value for every \(c\ge0\), takes the \(c=0\) count degeneration and Yata Gaussian formula as attributed background, derives the substantive continuity, monotonicity, Lipschitz, and infinite-audit frontier, specifies parameter-independent kernels in both directions with separate sign/count normalization, audited-cell binomial--Poisson, invalid-count/reconstruction, Gaussian jitter, and welfare-expansion debits, reduces four audit marks to two decision-relevant counts, and gives certified values, original-record attaining rules, and an explicit open strict-gain region.
